G L E U H R
Wellness Pvt Ltd


To our new Branch Manager
On joining GLEUHR — handed over by Harman
Dear [Name],
Welcome to GLEUHR. I am writing to you directly — separately from the formal onboarding pack — because the role you have stepped into is one of the most important in this company, and I want you to hear from me, in my words, what it actually means.
A Branch Manager at GLEUHR is not a supervisor of a clinic. She is the owner of one. The revenue of that branch, the operations of that branch, the quality of every client experience inside its four walls, the discipline of every team member who works in it — all of it sits with you. The brand has built its reputation one clinic at a time, and the difference between a branch that flourishes and one that drifts is almost entirely the quality of the BM who runs it. Nothing higher up matters if the branch is not held with seriousness on the ground. Holding it is your job.
I want to tell you how I think about this role. The BM owns two things together — branch revenue and branch operations. Most BMs in this industry think of themselves as primarily one or the other — either a sales manager who tolerates operations, or an operations manager who supports sales. Neither works. A branch with strong sales and weak operations starts losing clients within six months. A branch with strong operations and weak sales never grows. The two are the same job, done well, every day. If you have come from somewhere where these were split, unlearn that now.
There is a structure you are walking into, and I want you to understand it before tomorrow. You report to a Regional Head, who reports to the Chief Business Officer. Functionally, you work with Manisha on sales and with Saurabh on operations — both report to the CBO. The Regional Head visits your branch on a five-day cycle every month. They are your daily partner, not your monthly visitor. You also have one peer relationship inside the branch — the senior doctor. The doctor leads clinical, you lead the rest. The two of you meet daily, work as equals, and the minutes of every meeting go to corporate — to the Regional Head, to Manisha, and to Dr Kanikta who heads clinical for the company. This peer structure is not negotiable. The branches where the BM tries to manage the doctor, or where the doctor tries to manage the BM, are the branches that quietly fall apart. Different functions, same level, both reporting up. Hold that line.
Below you, you have the rest of the branch — reception, counsellors, housekeeping, therapists. You manage all of them. Each function has its own SOP and its own scorecard. You will be trained on every one. The training takes fourteen to twenty days at our Chandigarh branch — length depends on how quickly you absorb the work. You will be signed off as ready when you can independently run a Chandigarh shift solo for three consecutive days, with every function — reception, counsellor, therapist, housekeeping, doctor coordination — operating to standard while you are in charge. Not before. We do not deploy half-trained BMs.
Here is what you can expect from me. I will not micromanage you. Once you are signed off, I trust you to run your branch. I will not call your team members directly without telling you first. I will not undercut you in front of anyone. The Regional Head is your day-to-day partner; she has my full backing. If I disagree with something she has done, I take it up with her, not around her. You do the same with your team.
Here is what I want from you. Be honest with your Regional Head, and through her with me, even when honesty is uncomfortable. Tell us a problem before we find it from somewhere else. Do not protect a counsellor or a receptionist who is failing — your loyalty is to the branch, not to the individuals who happen to report to you. Do not have favourites. Do not let one function inside the branch become your inner circle. Respect the doctor as a peer, even when you disagree clinically — and especially when she disagrees with you operationally. Adhere to leadership decisions. If you disagree, raise it with the Regional Head; once locked, you carry it down. Own every problem in your branch, even when its cause sits elsewhere. Never use another team as the shield for a gap in yours.
One more thing. Every month, you will prepare a Branch Growth Plan that goes to your Regional Head. Not a report on the past — a plan for the next month. What you will grow, how you will grow it, what is in your way, what you need from us. This is how you signal to me that you are not just running the branch — you are building it. The BMs whose Branch Growth Plans become more ambitious quarter on quarter are the BMs whose branches become the next training grounds for the company. Keep that horizon in mind.
Harman, who handed you this letter, knows every department and every function. She is my eyes across the company. If anything in your training is unclear, if you ever feel uncertain, if you observe something that does not feel right — Harman is the person you go to first. After Harman, your Regional Head. The chain is there to protect you and the company.
I will meet you at the end of training, with your Regional Head. Until then, work hard, listen well, and remember that what you are learning over these fourteen to twenty days at Chandigarh becomes the foundation of how you run your own branch for years afterwards. Make it count.
Welcome to the team.

With respect, and with high expectations,

Urminder Singh
Founder & Managing Director  ·  Gleuhr Wellness Pvt Ltd


Handed over by Harman (Head of Departments) on Day 1 of joining. Accompanied by the KRA/KPI document and the training framework.
